report:
The restricted scalar-Hopf recovery argument is substantiated, subject to the normalization clarifications below. It supplies a substantive sufficient condition and an actual nonanalytic recovery system on a manifold with unbounded upper mass. It does not establish the entire original completion criteria: the proposed transverse invariant has no proved general replacement-invariant or uniform-estimate formulation, and retaining the classical BMP theorem as a separate branch does not establish the requested specialization of such an extension. No complete obstruction example is supplied. These are unresolved scope obligations, not a concrete counterexample to the restricted theorem.

A: The quotient, elliptic fibration, invariant positive form and identity dh = −ds ∧ alpha check directly. The indispensable non-BMP assertion is supported by the actual [Xia–Zhang construction](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.21053v1), not merely its theorem statement. Its heat-kernel energy satisfies E_eta(t) = 2 eta² log(1/t) + O(eta²). The choice t = eta^(1/eta²) makes this diverge on a fixed base ball. The transport and cutoff estimates give an integrable Schur-complement deficit tending to zero; the final smooth base correction restores strict positivity without removing the fiber energy. The mass identity consequently gives divergent masses of actual smooth strict potentials. Each is bounded individually, so this establishes v_+(h) = infinity.

B: The envelope-closure argument works in an arbitrary smooth, possibly nonclosed background. Convolution and a smooth convex maximum preserve the common Hessian bound up to an error tending to zero. Countable-ball selection and finite maxima produce the required increasing sequence. On each local modification, its canonical envelope agrees with the pullback envelope off the exceptional set and therefore everywhere. Local L1 convergence upstairs preserves every divisorial lower bound; domination of one fixed competitor gives the reverse bound. Exact ideal retention then follows from local valuative characterization and strong openness. The relevant hypotheses are local psh hypotheses after bounded smooth correction, so no Kähler assumption is imported onto the Hopf manifold. The Boucksom PDF was not retrievable in full; the needed applications were independently reconstructed using the opened [BFJ paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0702487), [Guan–Zhou paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1401.7158) and [Demailly notes](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/source_files/pdf/trieste.pdf). The maximum formula follows from logarithmic growth characterization, and affine additivity from linearity of the current definition.

The fiber-envelope identity also checks over all competitors. Orbit suprema retain the prescribed ideals by the preceding closure argument. Their invariant canonical representatives descend. Testing the positive ambient current against smooth horizontal lifts annihilating beta, with positive fiber test densities, proves base positivity distributionally. This avoids restricting a singular current to a fiber. Demailly’s Hilbert-tensor-product argument covers all holomorphic germs; Fubini on lifted germs supplies the converse ideal-equality test.

G and C: Scalar compatibility gives equality of the positive-slice ideal classes only. Defining Psi_tau^xi by the complete envelope of an admissible scalar input makes the construction independent of delta and valid for every positive, including nonclosed, xi. Taking the maximum of an endpoint competitor or convex combination with the appropriate input restores exactly the target orders at every local divisor. This proves decrease and concavity, including exceptional divisors. Canonical regularization extends the inequalities through poles. Scalar squeezing proves metric-independent genuine limits, and the ambient limit-model hypothesis supplies the base model property. Thus the full base-system hypotheses needed by the task-granted BMP theorem are established. Bounded kappa-psh potentials have mass 1, so P² has BMP. Applying that theorem, then the fiber identity and nested-background closure, proves recovery for every finite tau and every positive ambient eta. No limiting ideal survival or finite ambient deficit is assumed.

D: Uniform L1 bounds make the negative hyperplane series genuine and nontrivial. Its positive orders on infinitely many distinct hyperplanes exclude analytic singularity data. The proposed full envelopes satisfy normalization, compatibility, decrease and concavity by the verified closure and maximum arguments. Their decreasing limits retain the input orders by semicontinuity and domination, hence are exactly the unperturbed ideal envelopes. The strict-current bound and [non-pluripolar multilinearity](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0812.3674) yield initial input mass at least (1−lambda0)². [Witt Nyström’s theorem](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1703.01950v1) applies on the closed Kähler base without an analytic-singularity assumption. It transfers the bound to the model and, applied in both ordinary-order directions, proves the same mass for every ordinarily equivalent competitor. This establishes the claimed lower type volume, not an ambient raw-mass surrogate.

E and F: The base-modification statement is valid for the declared compact Kähler modifications with the exact pulled closed background. Pulled-background potentials descend by local psh extension and canonical uniqueness; ordinary types therefore correspond. Non-pluripolar measures agree off exceptional sets and charge neither those sets nor their images. [Darvas–Xia Lemma 3.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.03827) gives the matching envelope transformation. Its ideal-order envelope convention agrees here with the equality convention by taking a maximum with the admissible input and using closure. Demailly’s modification formula includes the relative canonical/Jacobian correction; it is not an uncorrected ideal-pullback formula. Arbitrary ambient modifications preserve the pulled divisorial constraints, but the proof supplies neither nonclosed numerical-volume invariance nor recovery for arbitrary new perturbation systems. Gauge transport is correctly used only after recovery has been proved. Existing valuative, concavity and modification results constitute substantial literature overlap; no priority conclusion follows from this audit.

Two harmless corrections are necessary. First, the supporting note’s instruction to divide both potentials and forms by 2pi should say to divide the background form while keeping each potential unchanged: h + D phi = (omega + D_source phi)/(2pi), giving mass scale (2pi)^−3. The main manuscript already uses this scaling. Second, the displayed order estimate uses function Lelong normalization nu(log|z|)=1. If nu denotes the coefficient of [F] in the task’s D phi instead, replace nu there by 2nu. The comparisons used in the proof are unchanged. Historical conditional implications do not establish their antecedents; the new lemma discharges the full-base-system antecedent only in the stated threefold setting. Completing the broader original invariant, estimates and specialization obligations would require an additional argument.

passages.statement: On X = (C³ minus {0})/<z maps to e^(-1)z>, with D_source = i partial barpartial, s = log|z|² and omega = i partial barpartial s + i partial s wedge barpartial s, Xia–Zhang Theorem 1.1 constructs smooth real phi_j with omega + D_source phi_j > 0 and integral_X(omega + D_source phi_j)^3 tending to infinity.

For a local psh function phi, J(phi) defined using exp(-2phi), every local prime divisor F on a smooth modification and every positive integer k satisfy nu_F(phi) − A(F)/k <= ord_F J(k phi)/k <= nu_F(phi), where nu(log|z|)=1 and A(F) is the finite log discrepancy.

For psh germs u,v at the origin of C^n, equality of their pointwise Lelong numbers at every point over the origin on every proper smooth modification is equivalent to J_+(tu)=J_+(tv) for every t>0, where J_+(w) is the stationary value of J((1+epsilon)w) as epsilon decreases to zero.
Strong openness holds locally for every psh weight phi: I(phi)=union_(epsilon>0) I((1+epsilon)phi), with I(phi) defined by local integrability of |f|² exp(-phi).

If psh functions converge locally in L1, the limiting Lelong number is at least the limsup of their Lelong numbers; the generic Lelong number along a prime divisor is the infimum of its pointwise Lelong numbers on the regular locus.

For a psh weight phi, its multiplier ideal J(phi), defined using exp(-2phi), is coherent; on a bounded Stein open set it is generated by any Hilbert basis of the weighted holomorphic L2 space.
For a holomorphic submersion f and a genuine local quasi-psh function u, I(t f* u)=f*I(tu) O for every real t>0, using exp(-tu).

For a proper generically one-to-one holomorphic map mu:Y→X of smooth complex manifolds and a psh function phi on X, mu_*(O(K_Y) tensor J(phi composed with mu))=O(K_X) tensor J(phi), where J uses exp(-2phi).
